title: Post in Fort Dodge Neighbors Talk: "RUN OUT of IV Fluids"

fields.avatarBrief: woman in her late thirties with a ponytail, smiling selfie in a car with a high school football hoodie
fields.text: My sister works at Prairie Ridge and says they have RUN OUT of IV fluids and are cancelling surgeries!! My dad's knee replacement is Wednesday. Does anyone know anything?? #FortDodge #PrairieRidge

comments.author: Travis K.
comments.text: My cousin drives freight out of Des Moines, heard it was the main plant that makes like 60% of all the bags. Got flattened in the storm last night. Nobody's getting any.

comments.author: Denise W.
comments.text: My mom has chemo at the infusion center Thursday. Nobody has called us. Should we drive to Ames??

comments.author: Gary L.
comments.text: Called the main number and got put on hold. That tells you something. Sharing so people know.

instructorNote: This is the misinformation inject. Hand out the post, then read aloud the 08:38 phone slip from the North Iowa NewsChannel assignment desk (on camera for the noon live hit; are surgeries being cancelled; which company is to blame) and the Patient Relations email (11 calls since 08:15 from Wednesday surgery and infusion patients). Watch whether the PIO puts out a same-day correction that the IC signs off on and that names no vendor, says emergency, urgent surgery and obstetric care continue, tells patients who to call and when the next update comes, and gives Patient Relations and the infusion center a call script that matches the clinical message.

mediaBrief.imagePrompt: Candid smartphone snapshot, slight tilt, natural color balance, neutral white balance. Candid phone snapshot taken from the hallway of a small Midwestern hospital surgical pre-op waiting area early on a weekday morning. Several worried family members sit in padded chairs, an older man in a flannel shirt with a knee brace beside his adult daughter, both looking at a phone. In the background, through plain glass, an empty IV pole stands beside a vacant stretcher, and a nurse in navy scrubs is seen from behind walking past. Plain beige walls, flat fluorescent ceiling light mixed with grey October daylight from a window, slight tilt, mild flash glare on the floor, uneasy, uncertain mood. Setting: a hospital loading dock: a delivery van with its rear doors open, pallets of boxed fluids, a technician with a hand truck, overcast daylight
